### 2026-10-22 – # October 22 - Research on Euroracks

# October 22 - Research on Euroracks
I love music and I am trying to make it when I feel like it.
So for this project I decided to try and make a eurorack from scratch.

So...
## What did I do today?
During this session I did some research on how euroracks works in general. The part about them is that everyone of them are often unique and having their own modules, filters, etc.
I found an interesting guy that makes music like this and most of all, experiments. His site is called "[Look Mum No Computer](https://www.lookmumnocomputer.com/)".

Gives out a triangle and a saw wave:
![Eurorack_Oscilator](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/8iQdaOwcrYZr4ba8jsAlUZx1MLmtyDZ7/ead8c27b06071c792161303a216b06729e68750542357c55ddeb44d29b5a9639.png)

Mixes waves coming from different modules into a single output:
![Eurorack_Mixer](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/8iQdaOwcrYZr4ba8jsAlUZx1MLmtyDZ7/62f24026a424d5db4c8ac0d8ad79af49b0fc58b40eb471164f41fd8f8701fb53.png)

## Parts needed so far
I also did some research on how to get signals out and so I had to measure my mixer that I have going to my speakers.

Measurement: 6.3 - 6.35mm TRS jacks.

![Eurorack_AudioJacks](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/8iQdaOwcrYZr4ba8jsAlUZx1MLmtyDZ7/214232d6af7caf53b5a5a4e4656ca478302b8682891423a05f4f190e23f89f7a.png)

### 2026-10-25 – # October 26 - Finished analog Eurorack Design!

**8.05h**

# October 26 - Finished analog Eurorack Design!
## What did I do
During this session I underwent a painfull process. First I found the last components that I will need (As long as I have not missed any). Secondly, I managed to map out my SSI2130 (oscillator) that will produce a customizable sound, where the customization comes from the controllable potentiometers aswell as incoming signals via "patch cables" that can be redirected by hand.

Wiring everything on the PCB too way to long. I did not know on before hand how much it would become and because I wanted a pretty compact design it lead to me trying to move different components, some with parts of a millimeter just so that they would fit.

## Schematic
I finished the schematic. I found a downloadable footprint aswell as the 3D model. Imported those to kicad and then wired everything together with a few resistors, potentiometers, capacitors here and there where they are needed.

## PCB
I created a PCB for my analog synth so that I have something to attach all my components to. I managed to fit most of the components in convenient spots and a few are placed just "where they ended up fitting".
Wiring everything on the PCB has easly taken me like (3-4)+ hours and that is just because I had duplicate of 2 components and then again, the cables needs to go through multiple components and most of the cables carries different signals meaning that they may not be crossed by each other.
